=== RESEARCH COMPLETE ===

Integrations Researched: 6
- OpenSSL: Verified ✓ (already a dependency)
- libmicrohttpd: Verified ✓ (⚠ CRITICAL ISSUE FOUND)
- libcurl: Verified ✓ (already a dependency)
- Puppet SSL/TLS Implementation: Verified ✓ (reference)
- Docker Certificate Management: Verified ✓
- Debian Package SSL Management: Verified ✓

Unverified Claims: 0

CRITICAL ISSUES: 1
⚠️  libmicrohttpd TLS Backend Incompatibility:
   - libmicrohttpd ONLY supports GnuTLS for TLS, NOT OpenSSL
   - Requirements explicitly state: "do not use gnutls"
   - IMPACT: Cannot add TLS to existing server without either:
     1. Violating requirements by adding GnuTLS
     2. Replacing libmicrohttpd with different HTTP server
     3. Implementing custom SSL socket wrapping
   - RECOMMENDATION: Consult stakeholders to resolve before implementation

Key Findings:

✅ Agent (Client) Side Ready:
   - libcurl already configured with OpenSSL support
   - Client certificate authentication well-documented
   - APIs: CURLOPT_SSLCERT, CURLOPT_SSLKEY, CURLOPT_CAINFO

⚠️  Server Side Blocked:
   - Current HTTP server (libmicrohttpd) requires GnuTLS for TLS
   - Conflicts with "do not use gnutls" requirement
   - Needs architectural decision

✅ OpenSSL Certificate Operations:
   - Already a dependency, used for crypto functions
   - Well-documented C APIs for X509 certificate generation/signing
   - Reference implementation available (github.com/zozs/openssl-sign-by-ca)

✅ Puppet SSL Workflow Documented:
   - 3 autosign modes: naive, basic (whitelist), policy-based
   - Certificate workflow: CSR submission -> CA signing -> certificate retrieval
   - Best practice: Use policy-based autosigning for security

✅ Deployment Patterns Clear:
   - Docker: Use volume mounts, never bake certs into images
   - Debian: Use ssl-cert package utilities in postinst scripts

Recommendations:

1. 🔴 URGENT: Resolve libmicrohttpd/GnuTLS conflict with stakeholders
   
2. Consider options:
   - Option A: Add GnuTLS for server TLS (simplest but violates requirement)
   - Option B: Replace libmicrohttpd with custom OpenSSL-based HTTP server
   - Option C: Implement raw SSL socket wrapper (complex, error-prone)

3. Implement Puppet-compatible certificate workflow:
   - Agent generates CSR
   - Server signs CSR (manual or autosign)
   - Agent retrieves signed certificate
   - Mutual TLS authentication

4. Add new server endpoints:
   - POST /puppet/v4/certificate_request
   - GET /puppet/v4/certificate/<certname>
   - GET /puppet/v4/certificate_status
   - PUT /puppet/v4/certificate_status/<certname>

5. Certificate storage structure:
   Server: /etc/puppetc/ssl/ca/, /etc/puppetc/ssl/certs/, /etc/puppetc/ssl/private/
   Agent: /etc/puppetc/ssl/certs/<certname>.pem, /etc/puppetc/ssl/private/<certname>.pem

## Research Phase Complete ✓

I've successfully researched all external integrations and dependencies for adding SSL/TLS between agent and server. The findings have been documented in `research.json`.

### Summary

**Integrations Researched:** 6 components
- ✅ **OpenSSL** - Already a dependency, well-documented C APIs for SSL/TLS and certificate operations
- ✅ **libcurl** - Already configured, excellent OpenSSL support for client certificate authentication  
- ⚠️ **libmicrohttpd** - Verified but **CRITICAL ISSUE** discovered
- ✅ **Puppet SSL/TLS workflow** - Reference implementation documented
- ✅ **Docker certificate management** - Best practices identified
- ✅ **Debian packaging with SSL** - ssl-cert utilities and patterns documented

### 🔴 Critical Issue Discovered

**libmicrohttpd TLS Backend Incompatibility:**

The existing HTTP server library (libmicrohttpd) **only supports GnuTLS for TLS**, not OpenSSL. This directly conflicts with the requirement: *"OpenSSL is already a dependency, so do not use gnutls"*.

**Impact:** Cannot implement server-side TLS without either:
1. Adding GnuTLS (violates requirement)
2. Replacing libmicrohttpd with OpenSSL-based solution
3. Complex custom SSL socket wrapping

**Recommendation:** This architectural decision needs stakeholder input before proceeding to implementation planning.

### Key Research Sources

**OpenSSL SSL/TLS & Certificates:**
- [SSL/TLS Client - OpenSSL Wiki](https://wiki.openssl.org/index.php/SSL/TLS_Client)
- [ssl server client programming using openssl in c - Aticleworld](https://aticleworld.com/ssl-server-client-using-openssl-in-c/)
- [OpenSSL C API certificate signing example](https://github.com/zozs/openssl-sign-by-ca)

**libcurl Client Certificates:**
- [Client certificates - everything curl](https://everything.curl.dev/usingcurl/tls/clientcert.html)
- [CURLOPT_SSLCERT](https://curl.se/libcurl/c/CURLOPT_SSLCERT.html)
- [Using Mutual TLS on the Client Side with Curl](https://smallstep.com/hello-mtls/doc/client/curl)

**Puppet SSL Workflow:**
- [Autosigning certificate requests - Puppet](https://www.puppet.com/docs/puppet/8/ssl_autosign.html)
- [autosign.conf configuration](https://www.puppet.com/docs/puppet/6/config_file_autosign.html)
- [Puppet best practices - autosigning](https://github.com/puppetlabs/best-practices/blob/master/autosigning.md)

**Docker & Debian:**
- [Automating TLS certificate management in Docker](https://smallstep.com/blog/automate-docker-ssl-tls-certificates/)
- [Debian ssl-cert package](https://packages.debian.org/sid/ssl-cert)

All detailed findings, API patterns, gotchas, and implementation notes are in `research.json`.

# Specification: Add SSL/TLS Mutual Authentication Between Agent and Server

## Overview

This task implements mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication between the Puppet agent and server, matching real Puppet's security model. The implementation includes a shared Certificate Authority (CA), PKI infrastructure on the server side for signing client certificates, and configurable auto-signing capabilities. This ensures secure, authenticated communication between all agent-server interactions while maintaining behavioral parity with production Puppet deployments.

## Workflow Type

**Type**: feature

**Rationale**: This is a new security feature that adds substantial functionality to the existing agent-server communication architecture. It requires implementing certificate management infrastructure, modifying network communication layers, updating build/deployment artifacts, and introducing new configuration options.

## Task Scope

### Services Involved
- **puppetc-agent** (primary) - Client-side mTLS implementation, certificate request workflow
- **puppetc-server** (primary) - Server-side mTLS implementation, certificate signing service, PKI management
- **Docker build system** (integration) - Multi-stage Dockerfile updates for certificate management
- **Debian packaging** (integration) - Package dependencies and installation scripts
- **Vagrant/Multipass** (integration) - Development environment updates

1→# Specification: Add SSL/TLS Mutual Authentication Between Agent and Server
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→This task implements mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication between the Puppet agent and server, matching real Puppet's security model. The implementation includes a shared Certificate Authority (CA), PKI infrastructure on the server side for signing client certificates, and configurable auto-signing capabilities. This ensures secure, authenticated communication between all agent-server interactions while maintaining behavioral parity with production Puppet deployments.
     6→
     7→## Workflow Type
     8→
     9→**Type**: feature
    10→
    11→**Rationale**: This is a new security feature that adds substantial functionality to the existing agent-server communication architecture. It requires implementing certificate management infrastructure, modifying network communication layers, updating build/deployment artifacts, and introducing new configuration options.
    12→
    13→## Task Scope
    14→
    15→### Services Involved
    16→- **puppetc-agent** (primary) - Client-side mTLS implementation, certificate request workflow
    17→- **puppetc-server** (primary) - Server-side mTLS implementation, certificate signing service, PKI management
    18→- **Docker build system** (integration) - Multi-stage Dockerfile updates for certificate management
    19→- **Debian packaging** (integration) - Package dependencies and installation scripts
    20→- **Vagrant/Multipass** (integration) - Development environment updates
    21→
    22→### This Task Will:
    23→- [x] Implement mutual TLS authentication using OpenSSL on both agent and server
    24→- [x] Create shared CA infrastructure with certificate generation and signing capabilities
    25→- [x] Add certificate signing request (CSR) workflow where agents request certificates from server
    26→- [x] Implement configurable auto-signing feature (policy-based, whitelist, or naive modes)
    27→- [x] Modify libcurl (agent) to use client certificates for HTTPS connections
    28→- [x] Resolve libmicrohttpd/GnuTLS conflict and implement server-side HTTPS with OpenSSL
    29→- [x] Update Docker images to include CA setup and certificate management
    30→- [x] Update Debian packages for OpenSSL dependencies and certificate storage
    31→- [x] Update Vagrant and Multipass configurations for secure development environments
    32→- [x] Add certificate storage locations and lifecycle management
    33→- [x] Implement error handling for certificate validation failures
    34→
    35→### Out of Scope:
    36→- Certificate revocation lists (CRLs) or OCSP support
    37→- Certificate rotation/renewal automation
    38→- Integration with external PKI systems
    39→- Web UI for certificate management
    40→- Certificate fingerprint pinning beyond standard X.509 validation
    41→
    42→## Service Context
    43→
    44→### puppetc-agent
    45→
    46→**Tech Stack:**
    47→- Language: C
    48→- Framework: libcurl (OpenSSL variant)
    49→- Key directories: `agent/`, `common/`
    50→
    51→**Entry Point:** `agent/puppetc_agent.c`
    52→
    53→**How to Run:**
    54→```bash
    55→puppetc-agent -n  # noop mode
    56→puppetc-agent -a  # apply mode
    57→```
    58→
    59→**Port:** Client (connects to server on 8140)
    60→
    61→**Current Communication Pattern:**
    62→- Uses libcurl for HTTP POST to server
    63→- Sends facts and receives compiled catalogs
    64→- Currently HTTP-only (no encryption or authentication)
    65→
    66→### puppetc-server
    67→
    68→**Tech Stack:**
    69→- Language: C
    70→- Framework: libmicrohttpd (⚠️ GnuTLS-only for HTTPS)
    71→- Key directories: `server/`, `common/`
    72→
    73→**Entry Point:** `server/puppetc_server.c`
    74→
    75→**How to Run:**
    76→```bash
    77→puppetc-server -v -m /etc/puppet/modules -D /etc/puppet/hiera /etc/puppet
    78→```
    79→
    80→**Port:** 8140
    81→
    82→**Current API Endpoints:**
    83→- `GET /status` - Health check
    84→- `POST /puppet/v4/catalog` - Compile catalog
    85→
    86→## Critical Architecture Decision Required
    87→
    88→### libmicrohttpd TLS Limitation
    89→
    90→**Problem**: libmicrohttpd (current HTTP server library) ONLY supports GnuTLS for TLS, which directly conflicts with the OpenSSL requirement.
    91→
    92→**Options**:
    93→1. **Replace libmicrohttpd** with OpenSSL-compatible HTTP server library
    94→   - Options: libevhtp, libevent with evhttps, custom implementation
    95→   - Pro: Single TLS dependency (OpenSSL only)
    96→   - Con: Significant refactoring of server code
    97→
    98→2. **Accept dual TLS dependency** (OpenSSL + GnuTLS)
    99→   - OpenSSL for certificate operations
   100→   - GnuTLS for libmicrohttpd HTTPS
   101→   - Pro: Minimal code changes
   102→   - Con: Two TLS libraries in dependency tree, larger binary size
   103→
   104→3. **Fork/patch libmicrohttpd** for OpenSSL support
   105→   - Pro: Keeps libmicrohttpd API
   106→   - Con: Maintenance burden, complex undertaking
   107→
   108→**Recommended Approach**: Option 1 - Replace libmicrohttpd with a lightweight OpenSSL-compatible HTTP server library. This maintains architectural cleanliness and satisfies the strict OpenSSL-only requirement.
   109→
   110→## Files to Modify
   111→
   112→| File | Service | What to Change |
   113→|------|---------|---------------|
   114→| `agent/puppetc_agent.c` | agent | Add libcurl mTLS options: CURLOPT_SSLCERT, CURLOPT_SSLKEY, CURLOPT_CAINFO, SSL verification flags |
   115→| `server/puppetc_server.c` | server | Replace libmicrohttpd with OpenSSL-compatible HTTP server, add TLS context initialization, implement certificate validation |
   116→| `server/puppet_ca.c` (new) | server | Certificate Authority implementation: CA cert/key generation, CSR signing, certificate storage |
   117→| `server/puppet_autosign.c` (new) | server | Auto-signing logic: policy-based validation, whitelist checking, configuration parsing |
   118→| `common/puppet_ssl.c` (new) | common | Shared SSL/TLS utilities: OpenSSL initialization, certificate loading, validation helpers |
   119→| `include/puppet_ssl.h` (new) | common | Header for SSL utilities and structures |
   120→| `include/puppet_ca.h` (new) | server | Header for CA operations |
   121→| `configure.ac` | build | Add checks for new HTTP server library (if replacing libmicrohttpd) |
   122→| `Dockerfile` | docker | Add CA initialization steps, certificate directory creation, OpenSSL tools |
   123→| `docker-compose.yml` | docker | Add volume mounts for certificate storage, environment variables for CA paths |
   124→| `vagrant/Vagrantfile` | vagrant | Add certificate setup provisioning steps |
   125→| `multipass/cloud-init.yaml` | multipass | Add OpenSSL tools and certificate directory setup |
   126→| `debian/control` | debian | Update dependencies if replacing libmicrohttpd |
   127→| `debian/puppetc-server.postinst` (new) | debian | Post-installation script to initialize CA if not exists |
   128→| `debian/puppetc-agent.postinst` (new) | debian | Post-installation script to create certificate directories |
   129→
   130→## Files to Reference
   131→
   132→These files show patterns to follow:
   133→
   134→| File | Pattern to Copy |
   135→|------|----------------|
   136→| `compiler/puppet_stdlib.c` | OpenSSL EVP API usage for OpenSSL 3.0+ compatibility (lines 4290-4298, 4334-4342) |
   137→| `agent/puppetc_agent.c` | libcurl option setting pattern (lines 123-139, 192-196) |
   138→| `server/puppetc_server.c` | HTTP request handling pattern with MHD (lines 55-93) |
   139→| `common/config_parser.c` | Configuration file parsing pattern for new autosign config |
   140→| `Dockerfile` | Multi-stage build pattern (builder → server/agent) |
   141→
   142→## Patterns to Follow
   143→
   144→### OpenSSL EVP API (OpenSSL 3.0+ Compatible)
   145→
   146→From `compiler/puppet_stdlib.c`:
   147→
   148→```c
   149→/* Use EVP API (OpenSSL 3.0+ compatible) */
   150→unsigned char hash[EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE];
   151→unsigned int hash_len;
   152→EVP_MD_CTX *ctx = EVP_MD_CTX_new();
   153→if (ctx) {
   154→    EVP_DigestInit_ex(ctx, EVP_sha1(), NULL);
   155→    EVP_DigestUpdate(ctx, data, data_len);
   156→    EVP_DigestFinal_ex(ctx, hash, &hash_len);
   157→    EVP_MD_CTX_free(ctx);
   158→}
   159→```
   160→
   161→**Key Points:**
   162→- Use EVP API instead of deprecated SHA1(), MD5() functions
   163→- Always check ctx != NULL before use
   164→- Free context with EVP_MD_CTX_free() to prevent memory leaks
   165→- This pattern is compatible with both OpenSSL 1.1+ and 3.0+
   166→
   167→### libcurl TLS Configuration
   168→
   169→From `agent/puppetc_agent.c` (to be added):
   170→
   171→```c
   172→curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_SSLCERT, client_cert_path);
   173→curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_SSLKEY, client_key_path);
   174→curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_CAINFO, ca_cert_path);
   175→curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER, 1L);
   176→curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST, 2L);
   177→```
   178→
   179→**Key Points:**
   180→- Set all three cert paths: client cert, client key, CA cert
   181→- ALWAYS enable verification (VERIFYPEER=1, VERIFYHOST=2) for security
   182→- Proper error handling if certificates don't exist or are invalid
   183→
   184→### OpenSSL Initialization Pattern
   185→
   186→```c
   187→#include <openssl/ssl.h>
   188→#include <openssl/err.h>
   189→#include <openssl/x509.h>
   190→#include <openssl/x509v3.h>
   191→#include <openssl/pem.h>
   192→#include <openssl/rsa.h>
   193→#include <openssl/evp.h>
   194→
   195→/* Initialize OpenSSL (call once at startup) */
   196→void puppet_ssl_init(void) {
   197→    SSL_library_init();
   198→    SSL_load_error_strings();
   199→    OpenSSL_add_all_algorithms();
   200→}
   201→
   202→/* Cleanup OpenSSL (call at shutdown) */
   203→void puppet_ssl_cleanup(void) {
   204→    EVP_cleanup();
   205→    ERR_free_strings();
   206→}
   207→```
   208→
   209→**Key Points:**
   210→- Call initialization functions before any OpenSSL operations
   211→- Cleanup prevents memory leaks
   212→- Thread-safe in OpenSSL 1.

Perfect! All planning files have been successfully created. Here's a summary of what was accomplished:

## ✅ Planning Phase Complete

### Files Created

All planning artifacts have been created in `.auto-claude/specs/001-add-ssl-tls-between-agent-and-server/`:

1. **implementation_plan.json** (23KB) - Complete implementation plan with:
   - 9 phases organized by service dependencies
   - 27 subtasks with clear verification steps
   - Parallelism analysis (2 workers recommended)
   - Comprehensive verification strategy (critical risk level)
   - QA acceptance criteria

2. **project_index.json** (1.9KB) - Updated project structure:
   - Corrected to reflect C-based agent/server architecture
   - Autotools build system configuration
   - Service definitions for agent and server

3. **context.json** (2.8KB) - Updated task context:
   - Scoped services: agent, server
   - Files to modify and create
   - Critical architectural decisions (replace libmicrohttpd)
   - Existing code patterns to reference

4. **init.sh** (4.2KB, executable) - Environment setup script:
   - Dependency checking
   - Project build with autotools
   - Docker service startup
   - Verification steps

5. **build-progress.txt** (4.4KB) - Progress tracking document

### Implementation Plan Overview

**Workflow Type**: FEATURE (multi-service security implementation)

**Phase Structure** (9 phases, dependency-ordered):
1. **SSL Infrastructure** (common) - Foundation utilities → 2 subtasks
2. **Server CA** - Certificate Authority implementation → 3 subtasks
3. **Server HTTPS** - Replace libmicrohttpd, add TLS → 4 subtasks
4. **Agent mTLS** - Client certificate support → 3 subtasks
5. **Build System** - Autotools updates → 3 subtasks
6. **Docker Integration** - Images and compose → 3 subtasks
7. **Debian Packaging** - Packages and postinst scripts → 3 subtasks
8. **Dev Environments** - Vagrant/Multipass → 2 subtasks
9. **Integration Testing** - End-to-end verification → 4 subtasks

**Parallelism**: Max 3 phases can run concurrently at certain points
- Recommended workers: **2**
- Speedup estimate: **1.5x faster** than sequential

**Verification Strategy**:
- Risk level: **CRITICAL**
- Tests required: unit, integration, e2e, **security**
- Security scanning: **REQUIRED**
- Staging deployment: **REQUIRED**

### Critical Architectural Decision

**Problem**: libmicrohttpd (current HTTP server) only supports GnuTLS for HTTPS, conflicting with OpenSSL requirement.

**Solution**: Replace with OpenSSL-compatible HTTP server (libevhtp or libevent) to maintain single TLS dependency.

### Next Steps

To continue with implementation, run:

```bash
source auto-claude/.venv/bin/activate && python auto-claude/run.py --spec 001 --parallel 2
```

This will launch 2 coder agents to work on independent phases concurrently.

---

1→/**
     2→ * @file puppet_memory.h
     3→ * @brief Memory management and leak detection for Puppet C parser
     4→ *
     5→ * This module provides memory allocation tracking and debugging capabilities
     6→ * to help identify memory leaks and allocation issues in the parser.
     7→ *
     8→ * Features:
     9→ * - Allocation tracking with file/line information
    10→ * - Memory leak detection and reporting
    11→ * - Double-free detection
    12→ * - Memory usage statistics
    13→ * - Optional Valgrind integration
    14→ */
    15→
    16→#ifndef PUPPET_MEMORY_H
    17→#define PUPPET_MEMORY_H
    18→
    19→#include <stddef.h>
    20→#include <stdbool.h>
    21→
    22→/*
    23→ * ===========================================================================
    24→ * MEMORY TRACKING CONFIGURATION
    25→ * ===========================================================================
    26→ */
    27→
    28→/* Enable memory tracking in debug builds */
    29→#ifdef DEBUG
    30→#define PUPPET_MEMORY_TRACKING 1
    31→#else
    32→#define PUPPET_MEMORY_TRACKING 0
    33→#endif
    34→
    35→/* Enable detailed allocation info (file/line) */
    36→#define PUPPET_MEMORY_DEBUG_INFO 1
    37→
    38→/*
    39→ * ===========================================================================
    40→ * MEMORY ALLOCATION WRAPPERS
    41→ * ===========================================================================
    42→ */
    43→
    44→#if PUPPET_MEMORY_TRACKING
    45→
    46→/* Tracked allocation functions */
    47→void *puppet_malloc_tracked(size_t size, const char *file, int line);
    48→void *puppet_calloc_tracked(size_t nmemb, size_t size, const char *file, int line);
    49→void *puppet_realloc_tracked(void *ptr, size_t size, const char *file, int line);
    50→char *puppet_strdup_tracked(const char *s, const char *file, int line);
    51→void puppet_free_tracked(void *ptr, const char *file, int line);
    52→
    53→/* Convenience macros that automatically pass file/line info */
    54→#define puppet_malloc(size) puppet_malloc_tracked(size, __FILE__, __LINE__)
    55→#define puppet_calloc(nmemb, size) puppet_calloc_tracked(nmemb, size, __FILE__, __LINE__)
    56→#define puppet_realloc(ptr, size) puppet_realloc_tracked(ptr, size, __FILE__, __LINE__)
    57→#define puppet_strdup(s) puppet_strdup_tracked(s, __FILE__, __LINE__)
    58→#define puppet_free(ptr) puppet_free_tracked(ptr, __FILE__, __LINE__)
    59→
    60→#else
    61→
    62→/* Direct system calls when tracking is disabled */
    63→#include <stdlib.h>
    64→#include <string.h>
    65→#define puppet_malloc(size) malloc(size)
    66→#define puppet_calloc(nmemb, size) calloc(nmemb, size)
    67→#define puppet_realloc(ptr, size) realloc(ptr, size)
    68→#define puppet_strdup(s) strdup(s)
    69→#define puppet_free(ptr) free(ptr)
    70→
    71→#endif /* PUPPET_MEMORY_TRACKING */
    72→
    73→/*
    74→ * ===========================================================================
    75→ * MEMORY TRACKING API
    76→ * ===========================================================================
    77→ */
    78→
    79→/**
    80→ * @brief Memory allocation statistics
    81→ */
    82→typedef struct puppet_memory_stats {
    83→    size_t total_allocations;      /**< Total number of allocations */
    84→    size_t total_frees;           /**< Total number of frees */
    85→    size_t current_allocations;    /**< Currently active allocations */
    86→    size_t peak_allocations;      /**< Peak number of active allocations */
    87→    size_t total_bytes_allocated; /**< Total bytes ever allocated */
    88→    size_t current_bytes_used;    /**< Current bytes in use */
    89→    size_t peak_bytes_used;       /**< Peak memory usage */
    90→} puppet_memory_stats_t;
    91→
    92→/**
    93→ * @brief Initialize memory tracking system
    94→ * 
    95→ * Should be called once at program startup before any allocations.
    96→ */
    97→void puppet_memory_init(void);
    98→
    99→/**
   100→ * @brief Shutdown memory tracking and report leaks
   101→ * 
   102→ * Should be called at program exit. Reports any memory leaks
   103→ * and cleans up tracking structures.
   104→ * 
   105→ * @return Number of leaked allocations
   106→ */
   107→int puppet_memory_shutdown(void);
   108→
   109→/**
   110→ * @brief Get current memory usage statistics
   111→ * @param stats Pointer to stats structure to fill
   112→ */
   113→void puppet_memory_get_stats(puppet_memory_stats_t *stats);
   114→
   115→/**
   116→ * @brief Print current memory usage statistics
   117→ */
   118→void puppet_memory_print_stats(void);
   119→
   120→/**
   121→ * @brief Print all currently allocated memory blocks
   122→ * 
   123→ * Useful for debugging memory leaks. Shows file/line information
   124→ * if PUPPET_MEMORY_DEBUG_INFO is enabled.
   125→ */
   126→void puppet_memory_print_leaks(void);
   127→
   128→/**
   129→ * @brief Check if a pointer was allocated by our tracking system
   130→ * @param ptr Pointer to check
   131→ * @return true if tracked, false otherwise
   132→ */
   133→bool puppet_memory_is_tracked(void *ptr);
   134→
   135→/**
   136→ * @brief Enable/disable memory tracking at runtime
   137→ * @param enabled Whether to enable tracking
   138→ */
   139→void puppet_memory_set_tracking(bool enabled);
   140→
   141→/*
   142→ * ===========================================================================
   143→ * CONVENIENCE MACROS FOR COMMON PATTERNS
   144→ * ===========================================================================
   145→ */
   146→
   147→/**
   148→ * @brief Safe allocation with error checking
   149→ * 
   150→ * Allocates memory and exits program on failure.
   151→ * Should only be used where allocation failure is fatal.
   152→ */
   153→#define PUPPET_MALLOC_OR_DIE(size) ({ \
   154→    void *ptr = puppet_malloc(size); \
   155→    if (!ptr) { \
   156→        fprintf(stderr, "Fatal: Memory allocation failed at %s:%d (size=%zu)\n", __FILE__, __LINE__, (size_t)(size)); \
   157→        exit(1); \
   158→    } \
   159→    ptr; \
   160→})
   161→
   162→/**

1→# Specification: Add SSL/TLS Mutual Authentication Between Agent and Server
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→This task implements mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication between the Puppet agent and server, matching real Puppet's security model. The implementation includes a shared Certificate Authority (CA), PKI infrastructure on the server side for signing client certificates, and configurable auto-signing capabilities. This ensures secure, authenticated communication between all agent-server interactions while maintaining behavioral parity with production Puppet deployments.
     6→
     7→## Workflow Type
     8→
     9→**Type**: feature
    10→
    11→**Rationale**: This is a new security feature that adds substantial functionality to the existing agent-server communication architecture. It requires implementing certificate management infrastructure, modifying network communication layers, updating build/deployment artifacts, and introducing new configuration options.
    12→
    13→## Task Scope
    14→
    15→### Services Involved
    16→- **puppetc-agent** (primary) - Client-side mTLS implementation, certificate request workflow
    17→- **puppetc-server** (primary) - Server-side mTLS implementation, certificate signing service, PKI management
    18→- **Docker build system** (integration) - Multi-stage Dockerfile updates for certificate management
    19→- **Debian packaging** (integration) - Package dependencies and installation scripts
    20→- **Vagrant/Multipass** (integration) - Development environment updates
    21→
    22→### This Task Will:
    23→- [x] Implement mutual TLS authentication using OpenSSL on both agent and server
    24→- [x] Create shared CA infrastructure with certificate generation and signing capabilities
    25→- [x] Add certificate signing request (CSR) workflow where agents request certificates from server
    26→- [x] Implement configurable auto-signing feature (policy-based, whitelist, or naive modes)
    27→- [x] Modify libcurl (agent) to use client certificates for HTTPS connections

    61→**Current Communication Pattern:**

    65→
    66→### puppetc-server

    86→## Critical Architecture Decision Required
    87→
    88→### libmicrohttpd TLS Limitation
    89→
    90→**Problem**: libmicrohttpd (current HTTP server library) ONLY supports GnuTLS for TLS, which directly conflicts with the OpenSSL requirement.
    91→
    92→**Options**:
    93→1. **Replace libmicrohttpd** with OpenSSL-compatible HTTP server library
    94→   - Options: libevhtp, libevent with evhttps, custom implementation

    96→   - Con: Significant refactoring of server code

   101→   - Pro: Minimal code changes
   102→   - Con: Two TLS libraries in dependency tree, larger binary size
   103→
   104→3. **Fork/patch libmicrohttpd** for OpenSSL support
   105→   - Pro: Keeps libmicrohttpd API
   106→   - Con: Maintenance burden, complex undertaking
   107→
   108→**Recommended Approach**: Option 1 - Replace libmicrohttpd with a lightweight OpenSSL-compatible HTTP server library. This maintains architectural cleanliness and satisfies the strict OpenSSL-only requirement.

   149→/* Use EVP API (OpenSSL 3.0+ compatible) */
   150→unsigned char hash[EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE];
   151→unsigned int hash_len;
   152→EVP_MD_CTX *ctx = EVP_MD_CTX_new();
   153→if (ctx) {
   154→    EVP_DigestInit_ex(ctx, EVP_sha1(), NULL);

1→# Specification: Add SSL/TLS Mutual Authentication Between Agent and Server
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→This task implements mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication between the Puppet agent and server, matching real Puppet's security model. The implementation includes a shared Certificate Authority (CA), PKI infrastructure on the server side for signing client certificates, and configurable auto-signing capabilities. This ensures secure, authenticated communication between all agent-server interactions while maintaining behavioral parity with production Puppet deployments.
     6→
     7→## Workflow Type
     8→
     9→**Type**: feature
    10→
    11→**Rationale**: This is a new security feature that adds substantial functionality to the existing agent-server communication architecture. It requires implementing certificate management infrastructure, modifying network communication layers, updating build/deployment artifacts, and introducing new configuration options.
    12→
    13→## Task Scope
    14→
    15→### Services Involved
    16→- **puppetc-agent** (primary) - Client-side mTLS implementation, certificate request workflow
    17→- **puppetc-server** (primary) - Server-side mTLS implementation, certificate signing service, PKI management
    18→- **Docker build system** (integration) - Multi-stage Dockerfile updates for certificate management
    19→- **Debian packaging** (integration) - Package dependencies and installation scripts
    20→- **Vagrant/Multipass** (integration) - Development environment updates
    21→
    22→### This Task Will:
    23→- [x] Implement mutual TLS authentication using OpenSSL on both agent and server
    24→- [x] Create shared CA infrastructure with certificate generation and signing capabilities
    25→- [x] Add certificate signing request (CSR) workflow where agents request certificates from server
    26→- [x] Implement configurable auto-signing feature (policy-based, whitelist, or naive modes)
    27→- [x] Modify libcurl (agent) to use client certificates for HTTPS connections
    28→- [x] Resolve libmicrohttpd/GnuTLS conflict and implement server-side HTTPS with OpenSSL
    29→- [x] Update Docker images to include CA setup and certificate management
    30→- [x] Update Debian packages for OpenSSL dependencies and certificate storage
    31→- [x] Update Vagrant and Multipass configurations for secure development environments
    32→- [x] Add certificate storage locations and lifecycle management

    66→### puppetc-server

    86→## Critical Architecture Decision Required
    87→
    88→### libmicrohttpd TLS Limitation
    89→
    90→**Problem**: libmicrohttpd (current HTTP server library) ONLY supports GnuTLS for TLS, which directly conflicts with the OpenSSL requirement.
    91→
    92→**Options**:
    93→1. **Replace libmicrohttpd** with OpenSSL-compatible HTTP server library

   101→   - Pro: Minimal code changes
   102→   - Con: Two TLS libraries in dependency tree, larger binary size
   103→
   104→3. **Fork/patch libmicrohttpd** for OpenSSL support
   105→   - Pro: Keeps libmicrohttpd API
   106→   - Con: Maintenance burden, complex undertaking

   108→**Recommended Approach**: Option 1 - Replace libmicrohttpd with a lightweight OpenSSL-compatible HTTP server library. This maintains architectural cleanliness and satisfies the strict OpenSSL-only requirement.

   136→| `compiler/puppet_stdlib.c` | OpenSSL EVP API usage for OpenSSL 3.0+ compatibility (lines 4290-4298, 4334-4342) |

   142→## Patterns to Follow

   144→### OpenSSL EVP API (OpenSSL 3.0+ Compatible)
   145→
   146→From `compiler/puppet_stdlib.c`:
   147→
   148→```c
   149→/* Use EVP API (OpenSSL 3.0+ compatible) */
   150→unsigned char hash[EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE];
   151→unsigned int hash_len;
   152→EVP_MD_CTX *ctx = EVP_MD_CTX_new();
   153→if (ctx) {
   154→    EVP_DigestInit_ex(ctx, EVP_sha1(), NULL);
   155→    EVP_DigestUpdate(ctx, data, data_len);
   156→    EVP_DigestFinal_ex(ctx, hash, &hash_len);
   157→    EVP_MD_CTX_free(ctx);
   158→}
   159→```
   160→
   161→**Key Points:**
   162→- Use EVP API instead of deprecated SHA1(), MD5() functions
   163→- Always check ctx != NULL before use
   164→- Free context with EVP_MD_CTX_free() to prevent memory leaks
   165→- This pattern is compatible with both OpenSSL 1.1+ and 3.0+

   176→curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST, 2L);

   180→- Set all three cert paths: client cert, client key, CA cert

   184→### OpenSSL Initialization Pattern

   196→void puppet_ssl_init(void) {

   198→    SSL_load_error_strings();
   199→    OpenSSL_add_all_algorithms();

   203→void puppet_ssl_cleanup(void) {

   205→    ERR_free_strings();
   206→}

1→/**
     2→ * @file puppet_ca.h
     3→ * @brief Certificate Authority for Puppet C implementation
     4→ *
     5→ * This module provides Certificate Authority functionality for the Puppet server,
     6→ * including CA certificate generation, CSR signing, and certificate management.
     7→ *
     8→ * Features:
     9→ * - CA certificate and private key generation
    10→ * - Certificate signing request (CSR) handling
    11→ * - X.509 certificate signing with serial number management
    12→ * - Signed certificate storage and retrieval
    13→ * - Auto-signing policy support (policy-based, whitelist, naive)
    14→ * - OpenSSL EVP API for OpenSSL 3.0+ compatibility
    15→ */
    16→
    17→#ifndef PUPPET_CA_H
    18→#define PUPPET_CA_H
    19→
    20→#include <stdbool.h>
    21→#include <stddef.h>
    22→#include <time.h>
    23→#include <openssl/ssl.h>
    24→#include <openssl/err.h>
    25→#include <openssl/x509.h>
    26→#include <openssl/x509v3.h>
    27→#include <openssl/pem.h>
    28→#include <openssl/evp.h>
    29→#include <openssl/rsa.h>
    30→
    31→#ifdef __cplusplus
    32→extern "C" {
    33→#endif
    34→
    35→/*
    36→ * ===========================================================================
    37→ * CA CONFIGURATION
    38→ * ===========================================================================
    39→ */
    40→
    41→/**
    42→ * @brief Default CA certificate validity period (10 years)
    43→ */
    44→#define PUPPET_CA_VALIDITY_DAYS (365 * 10)
    45→
    46→/**
    47→ * @brief Default signed certificate validity period (5 years)
    48→ */
    49→#define PUPPET_CA_CERT_VALIDITY_DAYS (365 * 5)
    50→
    51→/**
    52→ * @brief Default RSA key size for CA and certificates
    53→ */
    54→#define PUPPET_CA_KEY_SIZE 2048
    55→
    56→/**
    57→ * @brief Maximum path length
    58→ */
    59→#define PUPPET_CA_MAX_PATH 4096
    60→
    61→/**
    62→ * @brief Maximum error message length
    63→ */
    64→#define PUPPET_CA_MAX_ERROR 256
    65→
    66→/**
    67→ * @brief Maximum certname (common name) length
    68→ */
    69→#define PUPPET_CA_MAX_CERTNAME 256
    70→
    71→/**
    72→ * @brief Serial number file name
    73→ */
    74→#define PUPPET_CA_SERIAL_FILE "serial"
    75→
    76→/**
    77→ * @brief CA certificate file name
    78→ */
    79→#define PUPPET_CA_CERT_FILE "ca_crt.pem"
    80→
    81→/**
    82→ * @brief CA private key file name
    83→ */
    84→#define PUPPET_CA_KEY_FILE "ca_key.pem"
    85→
    86→/**
    87→ * @brief Directory for signed certificates
    88→ */
    89→#define PUPPET_CA_SIGNED_DIR "signed"
    90→
    91→/*
    92→ * ===========================================================================
    93→ * DATA STRUCTURES
    94→ * ===========================================================================
    95→ */
    96→
    97→/**
    98→ * @brief Certificate Authority context
    99→ */
   100→typedef struct puppet_ca_ctx {
   101→    char *ca_dir;               /**< CA directory path (e.g., /etc/puppetc/ssl/ca) */
   102→    X509 *ca_cert;              /**< CA certificate */
   103→    EVP_PKEY *ca_key;           /**< CA private key */
   104→    long serial_number;         /**< Current serial number for certificate signing */
   105→    char last_error[PUPPET_CA_MAX_ERROR]; /**< Last error message */
   106→} puppet_ca_ctx_t;
   107→
   108→/**
   109→ * @brief Certificate signing request information
   110→ */
   111→typedef struct puppet_csr_info {
   112→    char *certname;             /**< Certificate name (CN from CSR) */
   113→    char *subject;              /**< Full subject DN */
   114→    char *public_key_pem;       /**< Public key in PEM format */
   115→    char *fingerprint;          /**< CSR fingerprint (SHA-256) */
   116→    time_t request_time;        /**< When the CSR was received */
   117→} puppet_csr_info_t;
   118→
   119→/**
   120→ * @brief Auto-signing policy modes
   121→ */
   122→typedef enum {
   123→    PUPPET_AUTOSIGN_NONE,       /**< No auto-signing (manual approval only) */
   124→    PUPPET_AUTOSIGN_NAIVE,      /**< Auto-sign all CSRs (insecure, testing only) */
   125→    PUPPET_AUTOSIGN_WHITELIST,  /**< Auto-sign if certname in whitelist file */
   126→    PUPPET_AUTOSIGN_POLICY      /**< Auto-sign based on policy executable */
   127→} puppet_autosign_mode_t;
   128→
   129→/**
   130→ * @brief Auto-signing configuration
   131→ */
   132→typedef struct puppet_autosign_config {
   133→    puppet_autosign_mode_t mode; /**< Auto-signing mode */
   134→    char *policy_path;          /**< Path to policy executable (for POLICY mode) */
   135→    char *whitelist_path;       /**< Path to whitelist file (for WHITELIST mode) */
   136→    char last_error[PUPPET_CA_MAX_ERROR]; /**< Last error message */
   137→} puppet_autosign_config_t;
   138→
   139→/*
   140→ * ===========================================================================
   141→ * CA INITIALIZATION AND CLEANUP
   142→ * ===========================================================================
   143→ */
   144→
   145→/**
   146→ * @brief Initialize a Certificate Authority context
   147→ *
   148→ * Creates a new CA context and loads existing CA certificate and private key
   149→ * if they exist. If they don't exist, the CA must be generated using
   150→ * puppet_ca_generate().
   151→ *
   152→ * @param ca_dir Path to CA directory (e.g., /etc/puppetc/ssl/ca)
   153→ * @return New CA context, or NULL on error
   154→ */
   155→puppet_ca_ctx_t *puppet_ca_init(const char *ca_dir);
   156→
   157→/**
   158→ * @brief Free a Certificate Authority context
   159→ *
   160→ * Releases all resources associated with a CA context.
   161→ *
   162→ * @param ctx CA context to free
   163→ */
   164→void puppet_ca_free(puppet_ca_ctx_t *ctx);
   165→
   166→/*
   167→ * ===========================================================================
   168→ * CA GENERATION AND MANAGEMENT
   169→ * ===========================================================================
   170→ */
   171→
   172→/**
   173→ * @brief Generate a new Certificate Authority
   174→ *
   175→ * Generates a new CA certificate and private key with the specified validity
   176→ * period. The CA certificate is self-signed and can be used to sign client
   177→ * certificates.
   178→ *
   179→ * @param ctx CA context
   180→ * @param subject CA subject DN (e.g., "CN=Puppet CA: puppet-server")
   181→ * @param validity_days Number of days the CA certificate is valid
   182→ * @return 0 on success, -1 on error
   183→ */
   184→int puppet_ca_generate(puppet_ca_ctx_t *ctx, const char *subject, int validity_days);
   185→
   186→/**
   187→ * @brief Load existing CA certificate and private key
   188→ *
   189→ * Loads the CA certificate and private key from disk.
   190→ *
   191→ * @param ctx CA context
   192→ * @return 0 on success, -1 on error
   193→ */
   194→int puppet_ca_load(puppet_ca_ctx_t *ctx);
   195→
   196→/**
   197→ * @brief Save CA certificate and private key to disk
   198→ *
   199→ * Saves the CA certificate and private key in PEM format.
   200→ * The private key is saved with 0600 permissions (owner read/write only).
   201→ *
   202→ * @param ctx CA context
   203→ * @return 0 on success, -1 on error
   204→ */
   205→int puppet_ca_save(puppet_ca_ctx_t *ctx);
   206→
   207→/**
   208→ * @brief Check if CA certificate and key exist
   209→ *
   210→ * Checks whether the CA certificate and private key files exist in the
   211→ * CA directory.
   212→ *
   213→ * @param ctx CA context
   214→ * @return true if both files exist, false otherwise
   215→ */
   216→bool puppet_ca_exists(puppet_ca_ctx_t *ctx);
   217→
   218→/*
   219→ * ===========================================================================
   220→ * CERTIFICATE SIGNING
   221→ * ===========================================================================
   222→ */
   223→
   224→/**
   225→ * @brief Sign a certificate signing request
   226→ *
   227→ * Signs a CSR and generates a signed X.509 certificate. The certificate
   228→ * will be valid for the specified number of days and will include the
   229→ * certname as the Common Name (CN).
   230→ *
   231→ * @param ctx CA context
   232→ * @param csr_pem CSR in PEM format
   233→ * @param certname Certificate name (used for storage and validation)
   234→ * @param validity_days Number of days the certificate is valid
   235→ * @param signed_cert_pem Output buffer for signed certificate in PEM format (caller must free)
   236→ * @return 0 on success, -1 on error
   237→ */
   238→int puppet_ca_sign_csr(puppet_ca_ctx_t *ctx,
   239→                       const char *csr_pem,
   240→                       const char *certname,
   241→                       int validity_days,
   242→                       char **signed_cert_pem);
   243→
   244→/**
   245→ * @brief Parse CSR and extract information
   246→ *
   247→ * Parses a certificate signing request and extracts useful information
   248→ * such as the certname (CN), subject DN, and public key.
   249→ *
   250→ * @param csr_pem CSR in PEM format
   251→ * @param info Output CSR information structure (caller must free with puppet_csr_info_free)
   252→ * @return 0 on success, -1 on error
   253→ */
   254→int puppet_ca_parse_csr(const char *csr_pem, puppet_csr_info_t **info);
   255→

1→# Specification: Add SSL/TLS Mutual Authentication Between Agent and Server
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→This task implements mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication between the Puppet agent and server, matching real Puppet's security model. The implementation includes a shared Certificate Authority (CA), PKI infrastructure on the server side for signing client certificates, and configurable auto-signing capabilities. This ensures secure, authenticated communication between all agent-server interactions while maintaining behavioral parity with production Puppet deployments.
     6→
     7→## Workflow Type
     8→
     9→**Type**: feature
    10→
    11→**Rationale**: This is a new security feature that adds substantial functionality to the existing agent-server communication architecture. It requires implementing certificate management infrastructure, modifying network communication layers, updating build/deployment artifacts, and introducing new configuration options.
    12→
    13→## Task Scope
    14→
    15→### Services Involved
    16→- **puppetc-agent** (primary) - Client-side mTLS implementation, certificate request workflow
    17→- **puppetc-server** (primary) - Server-side mTLS implementation, certificate signing service, PKI management
    18→- **Docker build system** (integration) - Multi-stage Dockerfile updates for certificate management
    19→- **Debian packaging** (integration) - Package dependencies and installation scripts
    20→- **Vagrant/Multipass** (integration) - Development environment updates
    21→
    22→### This Task Will:
    23→- [x] Implement mutual TLS authentication using OpenSSL on both agent and server
    24→- [x] Create shared CA infrastructure with certificate generation and signing capabilities
    25→- [x] Add certificate signing request (CSR) workflow where agents request certificates from server
    26→- [x] Implement configurable auto-signing feature (policy-based, whitelist, or naive modes)
    27→- [x] Modify libcurl (agent) to use client certificates for HTTPS connections
    28→- [x] Resolve libmicrohttpd/GnuTLS conflict and implement server-side HTTPS with OpenSSL
    29→- [x] Update Docker images to include CA setup and certificate management
    30→- [x] Update Debian packages for OpenSSL dependencies and certificate storage
    31→- [x] Update Vagrant and Multipass configurations for secure development environments
    32→- [x] Add certificate storage locations and lifecycle management
    33→- [x] Implement error handling for certificate validation failures
    34→
    35→### Out of Scope:
    36→- Certificate revocation lists (CRLs) or OCSP support
    37→- Certificate rotation/renewal automation
    38→- Integration with external PKI systems
    39→- Web UI for certificate management
    40→- Certificate fingerprint pinning beyond standard X.509 validation
    41→
    42→## Service Context
    43→
    44→### puppetc-agent
    45→
    46→**Tech Stack:**
    47→- Language: C
    48→- Framework: libcurl (OpenSSL variant)
    49→- Key directories: `agent/`, `common/`
    50→
    51→**Entry Point:** `agent/puppetc_agent.c`
    52→
    53→**How to Run:**
    54→```bash
    55→puppetc-agent -n  # noop mode
    56→puppetc-agent -a  # apply mode
    57→```
    58→
    59→**Port:** Client (connects to server on 8140)
    60→
    61→**Current Communication Pattern:**
    62→- Uses libcurl for HTTP POST to server
    63→- Sends facts and receives compiled catalogs
    64→- Currently HTTP-only (no encryption or authentication)
    65→
    66→### puppetc-server
    67→
    68→**Tech Stack:**
    69→- Language: C
    70→- Framework: libmicrohttpd (⚠️ GnuTLS-only for HTTPS)
    71→- Key directories: `server/`, `common/`
    72→
    73→**Entry Point:** `server/puppetc_server.c`
    74→
    75→**How to Run:**
    76→```bash
    77→puppetc-server -v -m /etc/puppet/modules -D /etc/puppet/hiera /etc/puppet
    78→```
    79→
    80→**Port:** 8140
    81→
    82→**Current API Endpoints:**
    83→- `GET /status` - Health check
    84→- `POST /puppet/v4/catalog` - Compile catalog
    85→
    86→## Critical Architecture Decision Required
    87→
    88→### libmicrohttpd TLS Limitation
    89→
    90→**Problem**: libmicrohttpd (current HTTP server library) ONLY supports GnuTLS for TLS, which directly conflicts with the OpenSSL requirement.
    91→
    92→**Options**:
    93→1. **Replace libmicrohttpd** with OpenSSL-compatible HTTP server library
    94→   - Options: libevhtp, libevent with evhttps, custom implementation
    95→   - Pro: Single TLS dependency (OpenSSL only)
    96→   - Con: Significant refactoring of server code
    97→
    98→2. **Accept dual TLS dependency** (OpenSSL + GnuTLS)
    99→   - OpenSSL for certificate operations
   100→   - GnuTLS for libmicrohttpd HTTPS
   101→   - Pro: Minimal code changes
   102→   - Con: Two TLS libraries in dependency tree, larger binary size
   103→
   104→3. **Fork/patch libmicrohttpd** for OpenSSL support
   105→   - Pro: Keeps libmicrohttpd API
   106→   - Con: Maintenance burden, complex undertaking
   107→
   108→**Recommended Approach**: Option 1 - Replace libmicrohttpd with a lightweight OpenSSL-compatible HTTP server library. This maintains architectural cleanliness and satisfies the strict OpenSSL-only requirement.
   109→

   111→
   112→| File | Service | What to Change |
   113→|------|---------|---------------|

   115→| `server/puppetc_server.c` | server | Replace libmicrohttpd with OpenSSL-compatible HTTP server, add TLS context initialization, implement certificate validation |
   116→| `server/puppet_ca.c` (new) | server | Certificate Authority implementation: CA cert/key generation, CSR signing, certificate storage |

   122→| `Dockerfile` | docker | Add CA initialization steps, certificate directory creation, OpenSSL tools |
   123→| `docker-compose.yml` | docker | Add volume mounts for certificate storage, environment variables for CA paths |
   124→| `vagrant/Vagrantfile` | vagrant | Add certificate setup provisioning steps |
   125→| `multipass/cloud-init.yaml` | multipass | Add OpenSSL tools and certificate directory setup |
   126→| `debian/control` | debian | Update dependencies if replacing libmicrohttpd |
   127→| `debian/puppetc-server.postinst` (new) | debian | Post-installation script to initialize CA if not exists |
   128→| `debian/puppetc-agent.postinst` (new) | debian | Post-installation script to create certificate directories |
   129→
   130→## Files to Reference
   131→
   132→These files show patterns to follow:
   133→
   134→| File | Pattern to Copy |
   135→|------|----------------|
   136→| `compiler/puppet_stdlib.c` | OpenSSL EVP API usage for OpenSSL 3.0+ compatibility (lines 4290-4298, 4334-4342) |
   137→| `agent/puppetc_agent.c` | libcurl option setting pattern (lines 123-139, 192-196) |
   138→| `server/puppetc_server.c` | HTTP request handling pattern with MHD (lines 55-93) |
   139→| `common/config_parser.c` | Configuration file parsing pattern for new autosign config |
   140→| `Dockerfile` | Multi-stage build pattern (builder → server/agent) |
   141→
   142→## Patterns to Follow
   143→
   144→### OpenSSL EVP API (OpenSSL 3.0+ Compatible)
   145→
   146→From `compiler/puppet_stdlib.c`:
   147→
   148→```c
   149→/* Use EVP API (OpenSSL 3.0+ compatible) */
   150→unsigned char hash[EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE];
   151→unsigned int hash_len;
   152→EVP_MD_CTX *ctx = EVP_MD_CTX_new();
   153→if (ctx) {
   154→    EVP_DigestInit_ex(ctx, EVP_sha1(), NULL);
   155→    EVP_DigestUpdate(ctx, data, data_len);
   156→    EVP_DigestFinal_ex(ctx, hash, &hash_len);
   157→    EVP_MD_CTX_free(ctx);
   158→}
   159→```
   160→
   161→**Key Points:**
   162→- Use EVP API instead of deprecated SHA1(), MD5() functions
   163→- Always check ctx != NULL before use
   164→- Free context with EVP_MD_CTX_free() to prevent memory leaks
   165→- This pattern is compatible with both OpenSSL 1.1+ and 3.0+
   166→

   168→
   169→From `agent/puppetc_agent.c` (to be added):

   173→curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_SSLKEY, client_key_path);
   174→curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_CAINFO, ca_cert_path);
   175→curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER, 1L);
   176→curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST, 2L);
   177→```
   178→
   179→**Key Points:**
   180→- Set all three cert paths: client cert, client key, CA cert
   181→- ALWAYS enable verification (VERIFYPEER=1, VERIFYHOST=2) for security
   182→- Proper error handling if certificates don't exist or are invalid
   183→
   184→### OpenSSL Initialization Pattern
   185→
   186→```c

   188→#include <openssl/err.h>

   190→#include <openssl/x509v3.h>
   191→#include <openssl/pem.h>

   206→}
   207→```

   210→- Call initialization functions before any OpenSSL operations

   212→- Thread-safe in OpenSSL 1.

## Summary

I refactored `puppetc_server.c` to use the new evhtp HTTP server library with TLS context initialization while maintaining backward compatibility with libmicrohttpd.

### Key Changes:

1. **Conditional Compilation Support**: Added `#ifdef HAVE_EVHTP` blocks to support both evhtp (with TLS) and libmicrohttpd (HTTP-only fallback)

2. **TLS Integration**:
   - Included `puppet_ssl.h` and `puppet_ca.h` headers
   - Added `puppet_ssl_ctx_t *ssl_ctx` global variable for SSL context
   - Called `puppet_ssl_init()` on startup to initialize OpenSSL
   - Created SSL context in server mode with `puppet_ssl_ctx_new(true)`
   - Passed SSL context to evhtp via `evhtp_ssl_init()`
   - Added proper cleanup with `puppet_ssl_ctx_free()`

3. **New evhtp Handlers**: Implemented all endpoints using evhtp API:
   - Status endpoint
   - Catalog compilation
   - File server (plugins and modules)
   - PuppetDB queries
   - CORS support

4. **Configuration**: Added `-C, --ca-dir` option for specifying CA directory path (default: `/etc/puppetc/ssl/ca`)

5. **Preserved Functionality**: All existing endpoints continue to work exactly as before, just with HTTPS support when evhtp is available

The refactoring maintains the existing code patterns, uses proper memory management (puppet_malloc/puppet_free), and includes comprehensive error handling. The server now supports HTTPS when compiled with `HAVE_EVHTP`, with HTTP-only mode as a fallback.

1→# Specification: Add SSL/TLS Mutual Authentication Between Agent and Server
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→This task implements mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication between the Puppet agent and server, matching real Puppet's security model. The implementation includes a shared Certificate Authority (CA), PKI infrastructure on the server side for signing client certificates, and configurable auto-signing capabilities. This ensures secure, authenticated communication between all agent-server interactions while maintaining behavioral parity with production Puppet deployments.
     6→
     7→## Workflow Type
     8→
     9→**Type**: feature
    10→
    11→**Rationale**: This is a new security feature that adds substantial functionality to the existing agent-server communication architecture. It requires implementing certificate management infrastructure, modifying network communication layers, updating build/deployment artifacts, and introducing new configuration options.
    12→
    13→## Task Scope
    14→
    15→### Services Involved
    16→- **puppetc-agent** (primary) - Client-side mTLS implementation, certificate request workflow
    17→- **puppetc-server** (primary) - Server-side mTLS implementation, certificate signing service, PKI management
    18→- **Docker build system** (integration) - Multi-stage Dockerfile updates for certificate management
    19→- **Debian packaging** (integration) - Package dependencies and installation scripts
    20→- **Vagrant/Multipass** (integration) - Development environment updates
    21→
    22→### This Task Will:
    23→- [x] Implement mutual TLS authentication using OpenSSL on both agent and server
    24→- [x] Create shared CA infrastructure with certificate generation and signing capabilities
    25→- [x] Add certificate signing request (CSR) workflow where agents request certificates from server
    26→- [x] Implement configurable auto-signing feature (policy-based, whitelist, or naive modes)
    27→- [x] Modify libcurl (agent) to use client certificates for HTTPS connections
    28→- [x] Resolve libmicrohttpd/GnuTLS conflict and implement server-side HTTPS with OpenSSL
    29→- [x] Update Docker images to include CA setup and certificate management
    30→- [x] Update Debian packages for OpenSSL dependencies and certificate storage
    31→- [x] Update Vagrant and Multipass configurations for secure development environments
    32→- [x] Add certificate storage locations and lifecycle management
    33→- [x] Implement error handling for certificate validation failures
    34→
    35→### Out of Scope:
    36→- Certificate revocation lists (CRLs) or OCSP support
    37→- Certificate rotation/renewal automation
    38→- Integration with external PKI systems
    39→- Web UI for certificate management
    40→- Certificate fingerprint pinning beyond standard X.509 validation
    41→
    42→## Service Context
    43→
    44→### puppetc-agent
    45→
    46→**Tech Stack:**
    47→- Language: C
    48→- Framework: libcurl (OpenSSL variant)
    49→- Key directories: `agent/`, `common/`
    50→

    52→
    53→**How to Run:**
    54→```bash
    55→puppetc-agent -n  # noop mode
    56→puppetc-agent -a  # apply mode
    57→```
    58→
    59→**Port:** Client (connects to server on 8140)
    60→
    61→**Current Communication Pattern:**
    62→- Uses libcurl for HTTP POST to server
    63→- Sends facts and receives compiled catalogs
    64→- Currently HTTP-only (no encryption or authentication)
    65→
    66→### puppetc-server
    67→
    68→**Tech Stack:**
    69→- Language: C
    70→- Framework: libmicrohttpd (⚠️ GnuTLS-only for HTTPS)
    71→- Key directories: `server/`, `common/`
    72→
    73→**Entry Point:** `server/puppetc_server.c`
    74→
    75→**How to Run:**
    76→```bash
    77→puppetc-server -v -m /etc/puppet/modules -D /etc/puppet/hiera /etc/puppet
    78→```
    79→
    80→**Port:** 8140
    81→
    82→**Current API Endpoints:**
    83→- `GET /status` - Health check
    84→- `POST /puppet/v4/catalog` - Compile catalog
    85→
    86→## Critical Architecture Decision Required
    87→
    88→### libmicrohttpd TLS Limitation
    89→
    90→**Problem**: libmicrohttpd (current HTTP server library) ONLY supports GnuTLS for TLS, which directly conflicts with the OpenSSL requirement.
    91→
    92→**Options**:
    93→1. **Replace libmicrohttpd** with OpenSSL-compatible HTTP server library
    94→   - Options: libevhtp, libevent with evhttps, custom implementation
    95→   - Pro: Single TLS dependency (OpenSSL only)
    96→   - Con: Significant refactoring of server code
    97→
    98→2. **Accept dual TLS dependency** (OpenSSL + GnuTLS)
    99→   - OpenSSL for certificate operations
   100→   - GnuTLS for libmicrohttpd HTTPS
   101→   - Pro: Minimal code changes
   102→   - Con: Two TLS libraries in dependency tree, larger binary size
   103→
   104→3. **Fork/patch libmicrohttpd** for OpenSSL support
   105→   - Pro: Keeps libmicrohttpd API
   106→   - Con: Maintenance burden, complex undertaking
   107→
   108→**Recommended Approach**: Option 1 - Replace libmicrohttpd with a lightweight OpenSSL-compatible HTTP server library. This maintains architectural cleanliness and satisfies the strict OpenSSL-only requirement.

   123→| `docker-compose.yml` | docker | Add volume mounts for certificate storage, environment variables for CA paths |
   124→| `vagrant/Vagrantfile` | vagrant | Add certificate setup provisioning steps |

   128→| `debian/puppetc-agent.postinst` (new) | debian | Post-installation script to create certificate directories |
   129→
   130→## Files to Reference
   131→
   132→These files show patterns to follow:
   133→
   134→| File | Pattern to Copy |
   135→|------|----------------|
   136→| `compiler/puppet_stdlib.c` | OpenSSL EVP API usage for OpenSSL 3.0+ compatibility (lines 4290-4298, 4334-4342) |
   137→| `agent/puppetc_agent.c` | libcurl option setting pattern (lines 123-139, 192-196) |
   138→| `server/puppetc_server.c` | HTTP request handling pattern with MHD (lines 55-93) |
   139→| `common/config_parser.c` | Configuration file parsing pattern for new autosign config |
   140→| `Dockerfile` | Multi-stage build pattern (builder → server/agent) |
   141→
   142→## Patterns to Follow
   143→
   144→### OpenSSL EVP API (OpenSSL 3.0+ Compatible)
   145→
   146→From `compiler/puppet_stdlib.c`:
   147→
   148→```c
   149→/* Use EVP API (OpenSSL 3.0+ compatible) */
   150→unsigned char hash[EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE];
   151→unsigned int hash_len;
   152→EVP_MD_CTX *ctx = EVP_MD_CTX_new();
   153→if (ctx) {
   154→    EVP_DigestInit_ex(ctx, EVP_sha1(), NULL);
   155→    EVP_DigestUpdate(ctx, data, data_len);
   156→    EVP_DigestFinal_ex(ctx, hash, &hash_len);
   157→    EVP_MD_CTX_free(ctx);
   158→}
   159→```
   160→
   161→**Key Points:**
   162→- Use EVP API instead of deprecated SHA1(), MD5() functions
   163→- Always check ctx != NULL before use
   164→- Free context with EVP_MD_CTX_free() to prevent memory leaks
   165→- This pattern is compatible with both OpenSSL 1.1+ and 3.0+
   166→
   167→### libcurl TLS Configuration
   168→
   169→From `agent/puppetc_agent.c` (to be added):
   170→
   171→```c
   172→curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_SSLCERT, client_cert_path);
   173→curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_SSLKEY, client_key_path);
   174→curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_CAINFO, ca_cert_path);
   175→curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER, 1L);
   176→curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST, 2L);
   177→```
   178→
   179→**Key Points:**
   180→- Set all three cert paths: client cert, client key, CA cert
   181→- ALWAYS enable verification (VERIFYPEER=1, VERIFYHOST=2) for security
   182→- Proper error handling if certificates don't exist or are invalid
   183→
   184→### OpenSSL Initialization Pattern
   185→
   186→```c
   187→#include <openssl/ssl.h>
   188→#include <openssl/err.h>
   189→#include <openssl/x509.h>
   190→#include <openssl/x509v3.h>
   191→#include <openssl/pem.h>
   192→#include <openssl/rsa.h>
   193→#include <openssl/evp.h>
   194→
   195→/* Initialize OpenSSL (call once at startup) */
   196→void puppet_ssl_init(void) {
   197→    SSL_library_init();
   198→    SSL_load_error_strings();
   199→    OpenSSL_add_all_algorithms();
   200→}
   201→
   202→/* Cleanup OpenSSL (call at shutdown) */
   203→void puppet_ssl_cleanup(void) {
   204→    EVP_cleanup();
   205→    ERR_free_strings();
   206→}
   207→```
   208→
   209→**Key Points:**
   210→- Call initialization functions before any OpenSSL operations
   211→- Cleanup prevents memory leaks
   212→- Thread-safe in OpenSSL 1.

## Summary

I implemented comprehensive CSR (Certificate Signing Request) generation and submission logic in the Puppet agent. This allows the agent to automatically request certificates from the server when it doesn't have one.

### Key Functions Implemented:

1. **`generate_private_key()`** - Generates a 2048-bit RSA private key using OpenSSL 3.0+ EVP API
   - Saves with restrictive permissions (0600)
   - Compatible with both OpenSSL 1.1+ and 3.0+

2. **`create_certificate_request()`** - Creates an X.509 Certificate Signing Request
   - Sets CN (Common Name) field with the agent's certname
   - Signs the CSR with the private key using SHA256

3. **`csr_to_pem()`** - Converts X509_REQ to PEM format string
   - Uses BIO memory buffer for efficient conversion

4. **`submit_certificate_request()`** - Submits CSR to server via HTTP POST
   - Sends to `/puppet-ca/v1/certificate_request/:certname` endpoint
   - Receives signed certificate and saves it with 0644 permissions
   - Uses libcurl following existing patterns

5. **`ensure_certificate()`** - Orchestrates the complete CSR workflow
   - Checks if certificate already exists
   - Creates SSL directories if needed
   - Generates or loads existing private key
   - Creates and submits CSR to server
   - Handles complete error scenarios

1→# Specification: Add SSL/TLS Mutual Authentication Between Agent and Server
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→This task implements mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication between the Puppet agent and server, matching real Puppet's security model. The implementation includes a shared Certificate Authority (CA), PKI infrastructure on the server side for signing client certificates, and configurable auto-signing capabilities. This ensures secure, authenticated communication between all agent-server interactions while maintaining behavioral parity with production Puppet deployments.
     6→
     7→## Workflow Type
     8→
     9→**Type**: feature
    10→
    11→**Rationale**: This is a new security feature that adds substantial functionality to the existing agent-server communication architecture. It requires implementing certificate management infrastructure, modifying network communication layers, updating build/deployment artifacts, and introducing new configuration options.
    12→
    13→## Task Scope
    14→
    15→### Services Involved
    16→- **puppetc-agent** (primary) - Client-side mTLS implementation, certificate request workflow
    17→- **puppetc-server** (primary) - Server-side mTLS implementation, certificate signing service, PKI management
    18→- **Docker build system** (integration) - Multi-stage Dockerfile updates for certificate management
    19→- **Debian packaging** (integration) - Package dependencies and installation scripts
    20→- **Vagrant/Multipass** (integration) - Development environment updates
    21→
    22→### This Task Will:
    23→- [x] Implement mutual TLS authentication using OpenSSL on both agent and server
    24→- [x] Create shared CA infrastructure with certificate generation and signing capabilities
    25→- [x] Add certificate signing request (CSR) workflow where agents request certificates from server
    26→- [x] Implement configurable auto-signing feature (policy-based, whitelist, or naive modes)
    27→- [x] Modify libcurl (agent) to use client certificates for HTTPS connections
    28→- [x] Resolve libmicrohttpd/GnuTLS conflict and implement server-side HTTPS with OpenSSL
    29→- [x] Update Docker images to include CA setup and certificate management
    30→- [x] Update Debian packages for OpenSSL dependencies and certificate storage
    31→- [x] Update Vagrant and Multipass configurations for secure development environments
    32→- [x] Add certificate storage locations and lifecycle management
    33→- [x] Implement error handling for certificate validation failures
    34→
    35→### Out of Scope:
    36→- Certificate revocation lists (CRLs) or OCSP support
    37→- Certificate rotation/renewal automation
    38→- Integration with external PKI systems
    39→- Web UI for certificate management
    40→- Certificate fingerprint pinning beyond standard X.509 validation
    41→
    42→## Service Context
    43→
    44→### puppetc-agent
    45→
    46→**Tech Stack:**
    47→- Language: C
    48→- Framework: libcurl (OpenSSL variant)
    49→- Key directories: `agent/`, `common/`
    50→
    51→**Entry Point:** `agent/puppetc_agent.c`
    52→
    53→**How to Run:**
    54→```bash
    55→puppetc-agent -n  # noop mode
    56→puppetc-agent -a  # apply mode
    57→```
    58→
    59→**Port:** Client (connects to server on 8140)
    60→
    61→**Current Communication Pattern:**
    62→- Uses libcurl for HTTP POST to server
    63→- Sends facts and receives compiled catalogs
    64→- Currently HTTP-only (no encryption or authentication)
    65→
    66→### puppetc-server
    67→
    68→**Tech Stack:**
    69→- Language: C
    70→- Framework: libmicrohttpd (⚠️ GnuTLS-only for HTTPS)
    71→- Key directories: `server/`, `common/`
    72→
    73→**Entry Point:** `server/puppetc_server.c`
    74→
    75→**How to Run:**
    76→```bash
    77→puppetc-server -v -m /etc/puppet/modules -D /etc/puppet/hiera /etc/puppet
    78→```
    79→
    80→**Port:** 8140
    81→
    82→**Current API Endpoints:**
    83→- `GET /status` - Health check
    84→- `POST /puppet/v4/catalog` - Compile catalog
    85→
    86→## Critical Architecture Decision Required
    87→
    88→### libmicrohttpd TLS Limitation
    89→
    90→**Problem**: libmicrohttpd (current HTTP server library) ONLY supports GnuTLS for TLS, which directly conflicts with the OpenSSL requirement.
    91→
    92→**Options**:
    93→1. **Replace libmicrohttpd** with OpenSSL-compatible HTTP server library
    94→   - Options: libevhtp, libevent with evhttps, custom implementation
    95→   - Pro: Single TLS dependency (OpenSSL only)
    96→   - Con: Significant refactoring of server code
    97→
    98→2. **Accept dual TLS dependency** (OpenSSL + GnuTLS)
    99→   - OpenSSL for certificate operations
   100→   - GnuTLS for libmicrohttpd HTTPS
   101→   - Pro: Minimal code changes
   102→   - Con: Two TLS libraries in dependency tree, larger binary size
   103→
   104→3. **Fork/patch libmicrohttpd** for OpenSSL support
   105→   - Pro: Keeps libmicrohttpd API
   106→   - Con: Maintenance burden, complex undertaking
   107→
   108→**Recommended Approach**: Option 1 - Replace libmicrohttpd with a lightweight OpenSSL-compatible HTTP server library. This maintains architectural cleanliness and satisfies the strict OpenSSL-only requirement.
   109→
   110→## Files to Modify
   111→
   112→| File | Service | What to Change |
   113→|------|---------|---------------|
   114→| `agent/puppetc_agent.c` | agent | Add libcurl mTLS options: CURLOPT_SSLCERT, CURLOPT_SSLKEY, CURLOPT_CAINFO, SSL verification flags |
   115→| `server/puppetc_server.c` | server | Replace libmicrohttpd with OpenSSL-compatible HTTP server, add TLS context initialization, implement certificate validation |
   116→| `server/puppet_ca.c` (new) | server | Certificate Authority implementation: CA cert/key generation, CSR signing, certificate storage |
   117→| `server/puppet_autosign.c` (new) | server | Auto-signing logic: policy-based validation, whitelist checking, configuration parsing |
   118→| `common/puppet_ssl.c` (new) | common | Shared SSL/TLS utilities: OpenSSL initialization, certificate loading, validation helpers |
   119→| `include/puppet_ssl.h` (new) | common | Header for SSL utilities and structures |
   120→| `include/puppet_ca.h` (new) | server | Header for CA operations |
   121→| `configure.ac` | build | Add checks for new HTTP server library (if replacing libmicrohttpd) |
   122→| `Dockerfile` | docker | Add CA initialization steps, certificate directory creation, OpenSSL tools |
   123→| `docker-compose.yml` | docker | Add volume mounts for certificate storage, environment variables for CA paths |
   124→| `vagrant/Vagrantfile` | vagrant | Add certificate setup provisioning steps |
   125→| `multipass/cloud-init.yaml` | multipass | Add OpenSSL tools and certificate directory setup |
   126→| `debian/control` | debian | Update dependencies if replacing libmicrohttpd |
   127→| `debian/puppetc-server.postinst` (new) | debian | Post-installation script to initialize CA if not exists |
   128→| `debian/puppetc-agent.postinst` (new) | debian | Post-installation script to create certificate directories |
   129→
   130→## Files to Reference
   131→
   132→These files show patterns to follow:
   133→
   134→| File | Pattern to Copy |
   135→|------|----------------|
   136→| `compiler/puppet_stdlib.c` | OpenSSL EVP API usage for OpenSSL 3.0+ compatibility (lines 4290-4298, 4334-4342) |
   137→| `agent/puppetc_agent.c` | libcurl option setting pattern (lines 123-139, 192-196) |
   138→| `server/puppetc_server.c` | HTTP request handling pattern with MHD (lines 55-93) |
   139→| `common/config_parser.c` | Configuration file parsing pattern for new autosign config |
   140→| `Dockerfile` | Multi-stage build pattern (builder → server/agent) |
   141→
   142→## Patterns to Follow
   143→
   144→### OpenSSL EVP API (OpenSSL 3.0+ Compatible)
   145→
   146→From `compiler/puppet_stdlib.c`:
   147→
   148→```c
   149→/* Use EVP API (OpenSSL 3.0+ compatible) */
   150→unsigned char hash[EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE];
   151→unsigned int hash_len;
   152→EVP_MD_CTX *ctx = EVP_MD_CTX_new();
   153→if (ctx) {
   154→    EVP_DigestInit_ex(ctx, EVP_sha1(), NULL);
   155→    EVP_DigestUpdate(ctx, data, data_len);
   156→    EVP_DigestFinal_ex(ctx, hash, &hash_len);
   157→    EVP_MD_CTX_free(ctx);
   158→}
   159→```
   160→
   161→**Key Points:**
   162→- Use EVP API instead of deprecated SHA1(), MD5() functions
   163→- Always check ctx != NULL before use
   164→- Free context with EVP_MD_CTX_free() to prevent memory leaks
   165→- This pattern is compatible with both OpenSSL 1.1+ and 3.0+
   166→
   167→### libcurl TLS Configuration
   168→
   169→From `agent/puppetc_agent.c` (to be added):
   170→
   171→```c
   172→curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_SSLCERT, client_cert_path);
   173→curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_SSLKEY, client_key_path);
   174→curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_CAINFO, ca_cert_path);
   175→curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER, 1L);
   176→curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST, 2L);
   177→```
   178→
   179→**Key Points:**
   180→- Set all three cert paths: client cert, client key, CA cert
   181→- ALWAYS enable verification (VERIFYPEER=1, VERIFYHOST=2) for security
   182→- Proper error handling if certificates don't exist or are invalid
   183→
   184→### OpenSSL Initialization Pattern
   185→
   186→```c
   187→#include <openssl/ssl.h>
   188→#include <openssl/err.h>
   189→#include <openssl/x509.h>
   190→#include <openssl/x509v3.h>
   191→#include <openssl/pem.h>
   192→#include <openssl/rsa.h>
   193→#include <openssl/evp.h>
   194→
   195→/* Initialize OpenSSL (call once at startup) */
   196→void puppet_ssl_init(void) {
   197→    SSL_library_init();
   198→    SSL_load_error_strings();
   199→    OpenSSL_add_all_algorithms();
   200→}
   201→
   202→/* Cleanup OpenSSL (call at shutdown) */
   203→void puppet_ssl_cleanup(void) {
   204→    EVP_cleanup();
   205→    ERR_free_strings();
   206→}
   207→```
   208→
   209→**Key Points:**
   210→- Call initialization functions before any OpenSSL operations
   211→- Cleanup prevents memory leaks
   212→- Thread-safe in OpenSSL 1.
